name: HDX HAPI v2: humanitarian needs
used_for: People in need per country (intersectoral, national level)
terms: See HDX / HAPI terms of use; credit OCHA and HDX
notes: Needs data is often a year behind the funding year; such rows are flagged.

name: HDX HAPI v2: funding
publisher: OCHA Centre for Humdata (HDX); data from OCHA FTS
used_for: Funding requirements and amounts received per appeal
terms: See HDX / HAPI terms of use; credit OCHA FTS
notes: Current year only; appeals with no requirement are dropped.

name: OCHA Financial Tracking Service public API
used_for: Who funds each crisis: donor country totals per recipient (flows grouped by donor country)
terms: Public API; credit OCHA FTS
notes: Counts only money given to one country (single flows). Money split across several countries is excluded to avoid double counting. Totals include money outside the formal appeal, so they are larger than the appeal funding.

name: GDELT Project DOC 2.0 API
used_for: Recent articles per crisis in English, in each country's main local language, and from outlets inside the country; outlet country; coverage mix. GDELT machine-translates other languages for matching, so English keywords find them
terms: Free and open; credit GDELT
notes: Rate limits are strict, so data arrives slowly. Windows longer than about a week return nothing (use 1 week). Titles are shown in the original language with optional on-device or Google Translate help.

name: World country outlines
used_for: Map shapes (drawn with the Equal Earth projection)
terms: Natural Earth is public domain
notes: Palestine appears as the West Bank only.

name: Hand-found people-in-need figures
publisher: OCHA / UNICEF / WFP / ECHO documents (see data/reference/manual_pin.csv)
used_for: Missing people-in-need figures for Palestine, Lebanon, Madagascar, Nepal, Viet Nam, Cuba and Pakistan (used) and Honduras (found, not used)
terms: Each row lists its own source URL
notes: Each figure was read in the original document on 2026-11-17 and matched against the funding total it should belong to (see verification_report.csv). Cuba and Pakistan were first set aside by mistake and corrected after this check. Honduras remains unresolved.

name: Humanitarian Action plan pages
used_for: Year-by-year people in need, targeted, requirements and funding per plan: used to check Viet Nam, Cuba and Pakistan
terms: Public site; credit OCHA
notes: Its figures matched our FTS funding data for Viet Nam, Cuba and Pakistan.

name: Country summaries
publisher: AidGap, written from OCHA 2026 plan pages and ReliefWeb headlines (data/reference/country_context.csv)
used_for: One short paragraph per country on what is happening; each is paraphrased from a document read on 2026-11-17, with its basis and link
terms: Paraphrased, not copied; OCHA content is licensed CC BY 4.0
notes: Fetched with src/fetch_context.py. Where a plan page had no readable English narrative the summary rests on the latest aid-sector headlines instead and says so. Refresh by re-running the fetch and rewriting the CSV.

name: Local news outlets (public RSS feeds)
publisher: About 58 news outlets based in the crisis countries (list in src/fetch_local_news.py)
used_for: Local headlines (title, link, date, outlet) in each outlet's own language, filtered for humanitarian keywords
terms: Public RSS feeds; headlines and links only, shown with attribution; sites that refused access (HTTP 401/403/429) were skipped; please check each outlet's terms before wide publication
notes: About 20 of 58 outlets had a readable feed with relevant items. State-run outlets (SANA, Cameroon Tribune, WAFA, Cubadebate, Granma, The Rising Nepal, Ukrinform) are labelled state-linked.

name: Background photograph: Food distribution at a refugee settlement, Uganda

terms: Marked Public domain on Wikimedia Commons (checked 2026-11-17); credited on the page
notes: Illustrates the topic of the section, not necessarily the country shown. Not an endorsement.

name: Verification report
used_for: Independent checks: funding vs FTS plans API; recomputed scores; hand-added figures read in source documents; dashboard files vs CSVs
terms: Our own output
notes: Run python src/verify_data.py to repeat. Documents are fetched with an honest client name; if a site refuses, the check is reported as unverified and never bypassed.

name: Where-to-donate pages
publisher: UNICEF, World Food Programme, International Rescue Committee, MSF, UNRWA, Charity Navigator, CharityWatch, OCHA FTS (see data/reference/donate_links.csv)
used_for: Links to relief organisations' country pages
terms: Links only. Not an endorsement or rating
notes: Each address was checked to load on the date shown. 'Loads' does not mean 'recommended'.

name: News Droughts News Floods and US Disaster Relief
publisher: Eisensee and Stromberg, Quarterly Journal of Economics (2007)
used_for: Research context: news coverage affects whether disaster relief is given
terms: Cited for context only
notes: Please check the exact finding before quoting it in the final write-up.

name: Suffering in Silence (annual report)
used_for: Planned: compare with the most under-reported crises list
terms: Cited for context only
notes: Not yet matched to our ranking.

name: Google News RSS
used_for: Considered for article lists
terms: The feed states it is for personal feed readers only; any other use is prohibited
notes: Not used because the terms forbid use on a public website.

name: ReliefWeb public RSS feeds
used_for: Latest 20 humanitarian reports per country (title, link, date, publisher); attention rate in reports per week
terms: Public feed; content belongs to its publishers; every item links to the original
notes: No key needed. The feed ignores page numbers, so only the latest 20 reports per country are available; their time span gives the rate. Language is guessed from the headline.

name: ReliefWeb API v2
used_for: Every report in the last 90 days that lists each crisis country (title, date, source, language, themes, link); attention rate in reports per week
terms: Approved app name (free); content belongs to its publishers; every item links to the original
notes: Replaced the public RSS feed (latest 20 only). A report counts for a country when the country is listed among its countries, so regional reports that name it are included. Run src/fetch_reliefweb_api.py.

name: Anthropic (Claude) API
used_for: Optional: stored English translations of non-English headlines (src/translate_titles.py)
terms: Paid per use; needs a key
notes: Not used yet. Without it the page shows original headlines with an on-device translate button and a Google Translate link.

name: OCHA FTS: funding by donor and year
used_for: Worldwide humanitarian funding per year (2022 to 2026) by donor country, and US funding to each ranked crisis in 2024 vs 2025 (src/fetch_donor_trend.py)
terms: Public API, no key; credit OCHA FTS
notes: Only what donors and agencies report; late reports mean the newest year is incomplete. Shows amounts given, not how well money was spent. Money given to several countries at once is not split by country.

name: World Bank: military expenditure (SIPRI)
publisher: World Bank; underlying data SIPRI Military Expenditure Database
used_for: Military spending 2024 and 2025 for the biggest aid donors, shown next to their humanitarian aid (src/fetch_donor_trend.py)
terms: World Bank open data (CC BY 4.0); credit World Bank and SIPRI
notes: Current US dollars. No figures for Qatar or the UAE. A comparison only; it does not show that one spending choice caused another.

name: INFORM Severity Index
publisher: EU Joint Research Centre (method), ACAPS (data and analysis), coordinated by OCHA
used_for: How severe each crisis is, 1 to 10, for 68 countries (October 2026 release); input to Neglect Score v2 (src/fetch_inform.py, src/gap_score_v2.py)
terms: CC BY 4.0: credit INFORM; meant for comparing crises globally, not for deciding a specific response
notes: Analyst judgement built from public sources, not a measurement. Does not rate Viet Nam, Mozambique, Nepal or Madagascar. Methodology report not yet read: the exact weights between its three groups of indicators are not described here.

name: UNHCR Refugee Data Finder + World Bank population
used_for: People displaced from each crisis country, abroad and inside it, end of 2025, as a share of its population (src/fetch_displacement.py); input to Neglect Score v2
terms: Free public APIs, no key; credit UNHCR and the World Bank (CC BY 4.0)
notes: UNHCR does not count Palestinians registered with UNRWA, so Palestine has no displacement figure and that measure is left out for it. Some IDP counts are old. UNHCR uses its own country codes (mapped from its /countries list).

name: R4V Regional Refugee and Migrant Response Plan 2026
used_for: People-in-need figures and requirements for Brazil, Chile, Ecuador, Peru, Mexico, Costa Rica, Panama, Dominican Republic, Trinidad and Tobago (data/reference/manual_pin.csv)
terms: Public plan document; cite R4V
notes: Read in the PDF (text extracted locally). Country requirements match FTS. Counts refugees, migrants, returnees and affected host communities.

name: UNHCR Iran Flash Refugee Response Plan March-May 2026
used_for: Iran people in need 1.65M and requirement $80M (manual_pin.csv)
terms: Public plan document; cite UNHCR
notes: Covers only three months; matches FTS $80M. Confidence low.

name: UNHCR Uganda Country Refugee Response Plan 2026 Prioritization
used_for: Uganda people in need 2.2M refugees (2.7M host community listed separately)
terms: Public plan document; cite UNHCR
notes: Document says $850M; FTS shows $828.7M, about 2.5% apart.

name: Rohingya Joint Response Plan 2026 update
publisher: Rohingya response coordination (UN agencies and NGOs)
used_for: Bangladesh people in need: highest sector figure 1,860,109 (Health)
terms: Public plan document; cite the JRP
notes: Plan gives people in need per sector, not one overall number; maximum across sectors used. Requirement $710.5M matches FTS.
